rule.message: `octoprint.server.admin_permission` was deprecated since 1.4.0 and has been removed.
rule.suggestion: Remove usage of `octoprint.server.admin_permission`.

rule.message: Plugin implements `SimpleApiPlugin` but does not override `is_api_protected()`. Until OctoPrint 2.1.0, the default implementation returns `False`, allowing unauthenticated access to `SimpleApi` endpoints.
rule.suggestion: Override `is_api_protected()` to explicitly return `True`. Note that this only controls authentication; you should also verify permissions explicitly in each API handler (e.g. `Permissions.PLUGIN_MYPLUGIN_ACCESS`).

rule.message: Plugin implements `TemplatePlugin` but does not override `is_template_autoescaped()`. Until OctoPrint 2.1.0, the default implementation returns `False`, exposing the templates to XSS via unescaped variables.
rule.suggestion: Override `is_template_autoescaped()` to return `True` and use the `safe` Jinja filter only for variables that legitimately need to render HTML. See https://faq.octoprint.org/plugin-autoescape.

rule.message: Knockout `html:` binding bound to a non-literal value in a Jinja/HTML template. The bound expression is rendered as raw HTML, so any attacker-controllable data flowing into it results in DOM XSS.
rule.suggestion: Prefer the Knockout `text:` binding, which renders the value as plain text and is safe by default. Use `html:` only when raw HTML output is strictly required, and only with values that are either fully static or that have been properly sanitized.

rule.message: `PNotify` invocation passing a non-literal value as `text` without `text_escape: true`. PNotify v2 (the version shipped with OctoPrint) renders `text` as raw HTML by default, so any attacker-controllable data flowing into it (push messages, backend errors, printer responses, etc.) results in DOM XSS.
rule.suggestion: Set `text_escape: true` in the PNotify options so the value is rendered as plain text. If the value must contain HTML, escape any user-controllable substring via `_.escape(...)` before interpolating it into the markup.
